people.name: Oskar Klein
people.extract: Oskar Benjamin Klein was a Swedish theoretical physicist now best remembered for the Klein-Gordon equation of relativistic quantum mechanics, the Kaluza-Klein theory, a unified field theory of gravitation and electromagnetism, and the Klein–Nishina cross section in quantum electrodynamics.
highlights: Best remembered for the Klein-Gordon equation.
Developed Kaluza-Klein theory, a unified field theory.
Known for the Klein–Nishina cross section.

people.name: John N. Mitchell
people.extract: John Newton Mitchell was the 67th attorney general of the United States under President Richard Nixon. He also was chairman of Nixon's 1968 and 1972 presidential campaigns. Prior to that, he had been a municipal bond lawyer and one of Nixon's associates. Mitchell was tried and convicted as a result of his involvement in the Watergate scandal.
highlights: 67th attorney general of the United States.
Chairman of Nixon's 1968 and 1972 presidential campaigns.
Convicted due to involvement in the Watergate scandal.

people.name: Margaret Lockwood
people.extract: Margaret Mary Day Lockwood was a British actress. One of Britain's most popular film stars of the 1930s and 1940s, her film appearances included The Lady Vanishes (1938), Night Train to Munich (1940), The Man in Grey (1943), and The Wicked Lady (1945). She was nominated for the BAFTA Award for Best British Actress for the 1955 film Cast a Dark Shadow. She also starred in the television series Justice (1971–1974). Ronald Bergan of The Guardian called her "one of the most beautiful, energetic, and spirited actresses in the history of British cinema."
highlights: British actress, popular film star of 1930s and 1940s.
Starred in films like The Lady Vanishes and The Wicked Lady.
Nominated for BAFTA Award for Cast a Dark Shadow.
